summaries.summary: The image illustrates the time course of acute appendicitis, showing four stages: Appendiceal obstruction/early appendicitis with visceral peritoneal irritation, Appendiceal distension, Irritation of parietal peritoneum (localised), and Perforation with generalized peritonitis and sepsis. The stage before irritation of parietal peritoneum is appendiceal distension, characterized by anorexia, vomiting, and malaise.
key_facts: Appendiceal obstruction/early appendicitis leads to visceral peritoneal irritation with periumbilical colicky pain.
Appendiceal distension follows, marked by anorexia, vomiting, and malaise.
Irritation of parietal peritoneum (localised) occurs after distension, with constant RIF pain and pain on coughing.
Perforation leads to generalized peritonitis and sepsis.
visible_text: Appendiceal obstruction/early appendicitis – visceral peritoneal irritation
